newsitem.title: USA: S. Carolina jobless rate rises to 4.8 pct in May.
newsitem.headline: S. Carolina jobless rate rises to 4.8 pct in May.

text.p: South Carolina's unemployment rate edged up to 4.8 percent in May from 4.6 percent in April, the state Employment Security Commission said Wednesday.
"A slight increase this time of year is not unusual for South Carolina," the commission's executive director, Joel Cassidy, said.
The only major sector losing jobs was government, which lost 300 jobs, Cassidy said.

Total nonfarm employment rose by 13,400 in May with most of the growth centered in trade, which added 6,100 jobs, and services, which added 4,800. Tourism was a major factor as the summer vacation season began.
Construction also benefitted from the warmer weather, adding 1,200 jobs in May.
Cassidy said South Carolina should continue to see relatively low unemployment in the immediate future.
Williamsburg County had the state's highest unemployment rate in May, 12.8 percent, while Beaufort County had the lowest, 1.9 percent.
